title: The Community Garden Debate: Privacy, Technology, and Social Change · 独立口语迁移
instructions: 先完成示范段的跟读诊断，再用不同人物、信息或立场录制自己的完整回答。示范与自由回答分别取证，服务未提供完整听音评阅时保持待评。
reference: In the small town of Riverton, a community garden was created five years ago. At first, only ten families used it. They grew vegetables and shared tools. Last year, the town council decided to add new technology: a website where people could book garden plots online, and a camera to watch the garden at night. The council said this would help more people use the garden safely. However, some gardeners were not happy. They worried that the camera would record their faces and that their personal information might be shared. Maria, a gardener for three years, said, “I think that the camera is a good idea for safety, but I am not sure that everyone understands how the website works.” The council organized a meeting to discuss the changes. At the meeting, Tom, a council member, explained, “We believe that the website will make booking easier. The camera will only record when there is movement at night.

Part 1
Do you use any apps or websites in your daily life?
How do you feel about cameras in public places?
Do you think technology makes life easier or more difficult?

Part 2
Describe a time when a group of people discussed a change in your community. You should say: what the change was; who was involved; what people's opinions were; and explain how the discussion ended.

Part 3
Why do some people worry about new technology?
How can communities make decisions that everyone accepts?
What rules should companies follow to protect privacy?
Do you think technology will bring people together or separate them?
